item.title: The Evening the Lights Went Out
item.summary: During a power cut in a mahalla, neighbours share light, tea and food, and a boy sees his street differently.
item.content_markdown:
Last winter, on a cold evening in January, the lights in our mahalla suddenly went out. I was doing my maths homework, and my mother was cooking soup. Everything was dark and very quiet. The fridge stopped, the TV stopped, and my phone had only ten per cent battery.

At first, I was a bit scared. Then I heard voices outside. Our neighbour, Uncle Rustam, was in the street with a big torch. "Is everyone OK?" he asked. His wife brought candles for the old woman who lives alone at the end of the street.

Our gas cooker still worked, so my mother finished the soup and invited three families to eat with us. We sat together in the kitchen with candles on the table. The adults told stories about their childhood, and the children played word games.

The electricity came back after three hours. Everyone cheered, but I felt a little sad. It was a better evening than most evenings with the TV. Now, I know the names of all the children on our street.
